parsed.explanation: Combined regime: a 2026 penal code effectively criminalises all consensual same-sex relations (up to 2 years), a 2016 pornography law punishes content suggesting same-sex relations (7 years), two provinces criminalise same-sex conduct and one applies caning to 'persons with gender disorder'. State threat-framing is documented at presidential level (Oct 2025 defence decree), explicitly tied to an Aug 2026 surge in vigilante attacks on trans women. Police raid LGBT gatherings (75 arrested, 2025) and a trans traveller died in custody after an extortion demand. No anti-discrimination protection, no death penalty documented for trans status, prosecution selective. State-tolerated targeting plus criminalisation places this in High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Only M/F markers recognised domestically; foreign trans documents' treatment at entry is not documented. Mismatch exposure at airport is implied by a documented 2022 airport arrest of a trans traveller but the stop was drug-related.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch could feed a secondary inspection where morality provisions or the new penal code become relevant; no entry-specific trans rule stated.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans traveller died in custody (Aug 2022) after alleged police beating and a US$100,000 extortion demand; police deny violence. Police raided a private villa in June 2025, arresting 75 people at a 'gay party' deemed lawful by critics. Provincial caning applied to same-sex conduct and to 'persons with gender disorder'.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: A 2015 police circular on SOGI hate speech and a 2009 regulation duty to protect minorities exist on paper; enforcement outcomes not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Raid or conduct-based arrest → custody where the documented extortion/beating pattern and birth-sex placement risks apply; new penal code supplies a charging route.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Aceh applies its own Islamic criminal code with religious police caning; 400+ local bylaws, with two cities fining trans women. Capital agency has since 2018 raided trans women and confined them in 'rehabilitation' centres — mainly resident-facing but shows official framing of trans existence as offence.
federal_state_facilities.protection: National police have refused to enforce local rules conflicting with national guarantees — application varies by locality.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Subnational rules layer onto the national penal code; a visitor in Aceh or a bylaw city faces both levels simultaneously.

care_services.exposure: No documented emergency-care denial to visitors; psychiatric association (2016) pathologises trans identity and recommends 'rehabilitation', signalling institutional hostility toward care-seeking.
care_services.interaction: Any medical event outing a traveller occurs within a professional culture that officially labels trans identity an illness.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: October 2025 presidential decree lists LGBTQ+ people among nonmilitary national-defence threats alongside separatism and terrorism; commentators tie it directly to an August 2026 surge in mob attacks on trans women. Officials called on parents to monitor children in 'this lifestyle' (July 2026); broadcasting and website bans; a 2025 bill to bar online LGBT content under discussion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitutional/Human Rights Law theoretical non-discrimination; a rescinded discriminatory job posting shows the human rights commission can intervene on paper.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State doctrine licenses both vigilante action and official raids; censorship raises outing probability via device or app checks.

minors_guardians.exposure: A traveller accompanying a minor is not specifically documented; officials' July 2026 appeal to parents to monitor children and documented abuse surges against LGBT students indicate a hostile climate around minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Official framing of LGBTQ people as a defence threat could intensify scrutiny of an openly trans traveller accompanied by a child.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented patterned escalation: vigilante mobs attacking transgender women (14–15 Aug 2026), explicitly linked to official rhetoric and the defence decree; militia sweeps in four cities; sustained documented discrimination/arrests since 2016 (94 cases in one 2026 count). No denominator available for a rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police circulars on SOGI hate speech and 2009 minority-protection duty exist; no outcomes documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State threat-framing converts street hostility into tolerated or tacitly endorsed violence against an identifiable foreign visitor.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No SOGI anti-discrimination law; a police officer's wrongful-outing claim was rejected on procedural grounds (2019). Oversight reports recurring violations without remedying them.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional non-discrimination theory; human-rights commission advice; police circulars — none shown operating for trans travellers.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Custodial death allegations remain contested with police denial, indicating remedies do not reach state conduct.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this case. Here there is no documented routine months-long pretrial custody, coerced-confession machinery, or capital provision applied to presentation; prosecution is selective and penalties top out at 2–7 years. Custodial death and extortion are documented but as a single case, not intake-record pattern.

Lower than this case. Vellandra's exposure is exclusion and humiliation with no arrest or credible custody. This dossier documents criminalisation carrying imprisonment, state-directed raids, caning in one province, a death in custody, and presidential-level threat-framing — severity well above administrative exclusion.

Far lower. Kestrel Isles' worst outcome is refused admission and returned transport. Here the traveller faces criminal charges, state-tolerated mob violence and venue raids; entry friction is not even the salient exposure.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a national criminalisation floor (2026 penal code, pornography law, two provincial statutes) overlaid with subnational religious enforcement (Aceh caning) and topped by presidential threat-framing that documented reporting directly connects to an August 2026 surge in mob attacks on trans women. The state is simultaneously perpetrator (raids, custody death with extortion allegations, 'rehabilitation' raids), licensor (defence decree, official rhetoric) and nominal protector (unenforced 2009/2015 circulars). No death penalty attaches to trans status and prosecution is selective, keeping this above the 0.15 band, but state-tolerated targeting plus imprisonment exposure holds it firmly in High Risk. Minor-specific exposure is undocumented.
